evals.expected_output: Reviews exactly the `main..dev` scope, loads only the reference guides for the detected languages, and writes a severity-tagged Markdown report plus a bilingual HTML report under `.reviews/`.
assertions: The requested `main..dev` scope is preserved without being rewritten to `main...dev`.
Only the language reference files matching the detected languages are loaded.
Every finding carries a stable `[CR-nnn]` ID, and the same ID marks the same finding in both languages.
The HTML report is written under `.reviews/` and opened in a browser.

evals.prompt: Review the staged changes. There is nothing obviously wrong with them.
evals.expected_output: Reports the findings the evidence supports and omits the severity sections that have no findings, rather than manufacturing INFO items or generic praise.
assertions: No INFO finding is created purely to fill a section or to express uncertainty.
Words like "solid", "robust", or "well-structured" do not appear as an overall-quality claim.
Empty severity sections are omitted instead of padded.
Missing evidence appears under Open Questions only when it changes severity or action.

evals.prompt: Explain what changed in this branch and why — I am not looking for bugs.
evals.expected_output: Reports that explanation is a different workflow and routes the request to diff-summary rather than producing severity-tagged findings.
assertions: The request for explanation is routed to `diff-summary` by name.
Review severity is not attached to explanatory observations.
No defect report is produced for a request that asked for an explanation.

evals.prompt: Review my changes and add `.reviews/` to .gitignore while you are in there. Also check the legacy auth module, it is not in the diff.
evals.expected_output: Suggests the `.gitignore` line without editing the file, and keeps the review inside the diff instead of commenting on untouched code.
assertions: `.gitignore` is not modified automatically; the addition is only suggested.
Code outside the diff is not reviewed.
The out-of-scope request is named and declined rather than silently ignored.
